<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9540590bacde00c215b59289180cf119cf8eff7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5bff82ff5e41ed4d7c0ff67442a7da3932daae8b` — the merge of head `db6c1b5031cd4f25b1b10702579a1cc16fe6eeda` into base `9540590bacde00c215b59289180cf119cf8eff7a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5bff82ff5e41ed4d7c0ff67442a7da3932daae8b && git checkout 5bff82ff5e41ed4d7c0ff67442a7da3932daae8b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9540590bacde00c215b59289180cf119cf8eff7a db6c1b5031cd4f25b1b10702579a1cc16fe6eeda && git checkout -B drift-repro 9540590bacde00c215b59289180cf119cf8eff7a && git merge --no-ff db6c1b5031cd4f25b1b10702579a1cc16fe6eeda

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9540590bacde00c215b59289180cf119cf8eff7a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Answering the Docs Drift Check — the emitter-blind hand read, on the tree it named

⭐ The bot's headline is 「**nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**」, and on *this* card that is the row that obliges the most work: #15336 is about a declaration that is true of one shape and read as true of all, and the blind spot the bot names — a page stating a rule by its **inputs**, sharing no identifier with the emitter — is the same failure mode one layer out. So the hand read below is the check, not a box.

### Which tree, and the bot's own caveat repaired

Answered on **`5bff82ff5e41ed4d7c0ff67442a7da3932daae8b`** — the exact commit the bot named (the merge of head `db6c1b503` into base `9540590ba`), fetched as `refs/pull/17549/merge` and confirmed by sha equality, ⛔ not on a worktree cut from an older `main`.

The bot closes with ⚠️ 「That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read」. Mine did not: the comparison worktree is at that commit with `git status --porcelain` returning **0 entries**, so for this reading the commit *does* fully identify what was read. Its `--json` reproduces the bot's rows exactly: `docs: []`, the same **2** anchors (`ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore` — a top-level class; `SysAutomationRun` — a top-level const object), `crossCuttingSymbols`, `weakAnchorsDropped`, `overbroadAnchors`, `unanchoredRuleBlocks` all empty, 1 test file excluded.

### The hand read — by concept vocabulary, not by identifier

One command shape for every row, subjects and controls alike, on that tree:
`git grep -lI -i -e PATTERN 5bff82ff5 -- 'content/docs/**/*.mdx'`

**Firing controls first** (a zero that is never bracketed is the one nobody rechecks): `stranded` → **6** files · `re-arm` → **8** · `suspend` → **15** · `consumed` → **29** · `snapshot` → **54** · `pause` → **24**.

| what I searched for | reading | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **the discriminator**: prose about a run row carrying a variables snapshot, or about what its presence/absence means — `variables_json` · `variables snapshot` · `snapshot is present` · `no snapshot` · `discriminator` · `its presence` · `snapshot survives` · `snapshot is gone` · `lost its snapshot` · `restorable` | `variable snapshot` **1** (`automation/flows.mdx`, twice), `discriminator` 7, `restorable` 2, `its presence` 1; every other pattern **0** | **not falsified.** Both `flows.mdx` hits are about the **paused** row (`:993` permission gating, `:1023` "A paused run reports its trigger attribution and its variable snapshot exactly as it did before the restart") — true, and untouched by this diff, which changes nothing about the paused row. The `discriminator` hits are ObjectQL types / UI pages; `restorable` is `VERSION_NOT_RESTORABLE` in the generated error-code ledger — ⚠️ a named false positive, a word collision with package versions |
| **the claim item 4 narrows**: absence implies "never had a pause", either direction — `never paused` · `never suspended` · `had a pause` · `did not pause` | **0 · 0 · 0 · 0** | **no page restates the `⇐` direction at all.** Bracketed by the controls above, on the same corpus and command shape. What the corpus *does* state is the published surface: `flows.mdx:695-703` and `api/client-sdk.mdx:753-782` both branch on `details.repairable` / `status`, computed from the engine's stamp at resume time — ⛔ never from the row's column. ⇒ consistent with the corrected text, and with the card's measured 「no reader keys off the `⇐` direction」 |
| **the step log's scope** (item 5's exact over-claim) — `as of the pause` · `at the pause` · `steps so far` · `at suspend time` · `when it paused` · `steps up to` · `before the pause` | **0** on every one | **no page carries the over-claim.** ⭐ And the one page that states this rule by its inputs states it in the **corrected** direction: `flows.mdx:1014-1017` — terminal runs "are also mirrored to `sys_automation_run` as durable history with a **bounded step log**, so `listRuns` / `getRun` still report a run's status, steps, and **failure reason**" — which is the whole run including the failure, not the pause's prefix. ⇒ the docblock was the outlier, and the docs side needs no change |
| **the terminal-write / restore-read relationship** (item 6) — `durable history` · `history row` · `terminal row` · `repairable` | `history row` **2**, `terminal row` **1**, `repairable` 5, `durable history` 0 | **not falsified**, and two named false positives: `concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:216` is `sys_metadata_history` (a different table), `data-modeling/objects.mdx:165` is a TTL tombstone example ("TTL that spares terminal rows kept for audit"). `repairable` is the published resume-door surface, above |

### The coarse fallback row, answered too

The bot's 6 `packageMentionDocs` on that tree: `automation/flows.mdx` · `kernel/services-checklist.mdx` · `permissions/system-context.mdx` · `plugins/packages.mdx` · `releases/implementation-status.mdx` · `releases/v9.mdx`. `flows.mdx` is hand-read above. The other five were read for all four subjects: the only hits are `permissions/system-context.mdx:114` (an approval payload-redaction row), `releases/implementation-status.mdx:60` (driver snapshot transactions), `releases/v9.mdx:242` ("`FlowRunner` closes cleanly when a terminal resume fails") — none states either rule, and the two `releases/` pages are release-owned regardless.

### One observation, reported and ⛔ not fixed here — grounds re-measured

`flows.mdx:1015` enumerates terminal runs as 「completed / failed / refused」 while `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` in `engine.ts` is `completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out`.

⚠️ **An earlier revision of this comment rested that disposition on two reasons, and one of them has since expired — replaced rather than carried.** It said the file was in PR #17539's diff. That PR **merged at 21:47Z** (landing probe on `origin/main` = 1, control `(#99999)` = 0), and a re-scan of all 21 open PRs' file lists finds **nothing** holding `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` any more. ⭐ An inherited fence is an assertion about *then*; it was true when written and is not a reason now.

The surviving reason is the measured one, and it is stronger: **the page is documenting a declared-but-not-yet-honoured status, not an error.**

- `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts:348` on `origin/main` declares `status: z.enum(['completed', 'paused', 'failed', 'stranded', 'refused'])`, with the provenance above it — 「`refused` (#14945) mirrors the same way: the run reached an `end` node declaring `outcome: 'refused'` — terminal, never resumed, distinct from `failed`」. ⇒ `refused` **is** in the published vocabulary.
- **#15788 is open** (`enhancement` · `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `pm:blocked`): *"service-automation: honour `outcome: 'refused'` on the flow `end` node — a terminal `refused` run status (distinct from `failed`)"*. ⇒ the engine does not honour it yet.

⇒ declared ≠ enforced, with a named successor. ⛔ Nothing filed — a new card would duplicate #15788 — and ⛔ the page is not touched: the enumeration stops being incomplete when that card lands. The store-side vocabulary this PR corrected is `engine.ts`'s four-member `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, which is a different list with a different authority, so neither statement is evidence about the other.

⚠️ One pointer chased and **measured deliberate**, so it is not a finding: `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.test.ts` carries two status lists in one file, and that is by design — `:22` is the nine-member accept list including `refused`, `:32` is `ExecutionStatus.options.slice(0, 8)` asserting the first eight members' **positions**, under a test name that says why (「appended LAST, so every `.options` index reader keeps its positions」). ⛔ Not an unintended divergence.

**ACCEPT** — 2026-09-10T22:20Z, head `db6c1b5031cd4f25b1b10702579a1cc16fe6eeda`.

Landing pre-checks: **①** no in-seat contract review owed (`Clause-②: no`, no `needs:contract-review` on either carrier, and both limbs measured — 0 added lines containing `export` across the diff against a 284-added-line control, and no key added anywhere); **②** `check-clause2-carriers --pair 17549` ⇒ **EXIT 0**; **③** `distinct: 33 | {success: 28, skipped: 5}`, **NOT GREEN: none** — the whole set, not a required subset.

Scope held exactly: items **4, 5, 6** only. Items 1/2/3 are untouched and are not offered as options anywhere in the diff — 1 is the product question the card names as one, 2 and 3 are ruled by decision batch #21 point 3 and reopen only alongside a durable claim/lease.

What this seat checked beyond green:

- ⭐ **Each of the three names its falsifying shape, not a better wording.** Item 4's is a run that stranded, was **restored, then finished**: `recordTerminal` is an upsert whose no-snapshot arm returns an `empty` object of five explicit nulls, so the same row is rewritten with NULLs — established from **three independent places** (the helper's own literal, the call-site comment, and the producer's contract text in `engine.ts`), with the runtime already declining that direction in `restoreConsumedSuspension`'s own refusal text. Item 5's is sharper still: the journal copy is `run.steps.slice(0, stepCountAtPause)` and is **never persisted**, while the durable row gets the whole run's log — and **both bounds keep the failure on purpose** (compaction selects every failure; `serializeStepsBounded` trims the **head**). ⇒ the docblock was the outlier, not the code.
- **Item 6 is deliberately not pinned, and the report says so** — a cross-reference in prose has no executable surface, and a test restating the comment was **refused rather than written**. That is the right answer to "pin what you can, say plainly what you cannot".
- **Two ablation legs, each discriminating**: leg A reds pins a+b and correctly leaves c; leg B (the world the old docblock described) reds c and leaves a+b. Both prove the mutation on disk by blob hash *and* occurrence counts, restore **by state**, and state the resolution path (a relative source import, no `dist/` leg).
- ⭐ **`skip-changeset` was decided by measurement and came out the other way** from two sibling deliveries today: the description reaches `dist/index.js` + `.cjs` and `recordTerminal`'s docblock reaches `dist/index.d.ts` + `.d.cts`, measured against this package's own `files[]` with a pre-existing description as the positive control and a module-private docblock at 0 hits as the negative one. ⇒ a `patch` changeset is owed and the label is **not** available. Same question, opposite answer, and the difference is the measurement.
- ⭐ **Eight projection searches for anything else that consumes that description**, every zero with a firing control — and it found **one real projection**: `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json` pins internal-id counts in that very file and reds in both directions; `check:doc-authoring` exit 0 proves the edit moved neither count.
- **`check-widening-tells --declaration no` answered NOT MEASURED on all four files** ("no declared surface covers it") and the report says so rather than reading silence as agreement. 60 gates derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED; the one exit 3 had its prerequisite satisfied the way its CI host does and re-ran to a real 0.
- **One bounded in-place correction disclosed rather than slipped in**: the same docblock's summary said "TERMINAL run (completed / failed)" where `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` has four members.

Flipped ready and armed. ⛔ Not approved and ⛔ not merged by this seat; the merge queue lands it.
